opAll.Comment: ALU operands from the CPU:\nACC → A, argument → B,\nthe decoder sets OP (1 = add, 2 = sub)
ALU core:\nall units compute in parallel,\nOP picks the result
OP decoder (one-hot):\n1=ADD  2=SUB  4=AND\n8=OR  16=XOR  32=NOT A
Result mux:\nboth Select outputs\nOR-merge into R

Flags:
Z = result is zero
C = carry (ADD)
N = negative (SUB)
ALU outputs:\nR = result\nZ, C, N = flags

Front panel:
RUN switch starts the CPU, Reset homes it.
Upload a .bin program via the file input.
Status: PC, OP, ARG, ACC + load/halt lamps

Control unit:
clock runs while RUN & !HALT & !LOADING.
Phase counter cycles 1..6 per instruction:
1 = latch instruction, 3 = execute, 5 = advance PC
(2, 4 and 6 give signals time to settle,
6 also resets the phase counter).
The interval value sets the CPU speed —
below ~5 signals no longer settle in time.
HALT flipflop: set by the\nHLT instruction, cleared by Reset

Loader: reads the uploaded file, two bytes
per instruction (opcode, argument).
The flipflop toggles per byte read and routes
even bytes to the opcode ROM, odd bytes to
the argument ROM. The counter is the target
address. LOADING pauses the CPU clock,
the repeater keeps it alive for the last write.
RST pulses on file upload or Reset button:\nclears PC, HALT, data RAM and the screen

Program memory: two ROMs share one address —
one holds opcodes, the other arguments.
While LOADING the address comes from the loader,
otherwise from the program counter.
A new upload clears both ROMs first.
Instruction register: phase 1\nlatches opcode + argument
Program counter: phase 5 increments,\na taken jump loads the argument instead,\nReset starts over at 0

Data memory (RAM):
address = instruction argument,
STA stores the accumulator there,
LDA reads it back, Reset clears all
Terminal: the OUT instruction prints the\naccumulator as an ASCII character,\nbyte 10 = newline, Reset clears the screen

Instruction decoder: the opcode is compared
against every instruction, exactly one line fires:
01 LDI  02 ADD  03 SUB  04 LDA  05 STA
06 JMP  07 JZ  08 JNZ  09 OUT  0A HLT  0B IN

Accumulator: phase 3 latches the selected
source — argument (LDI), ALU result
(ADD/SUB) or data memory (LDA).
ZF checks 'ACC == 0' live
(the open input reads as 0)
ALU op code:\n1 = add, 2 = subtract
Jumps: on JMP, JZ (ZF set) or JNZ (ZF clear)\nphase 5 loads the PC with the argument,\notherwise the PC increments

Program file format (.bin):
two bytes per instruction: opcode, argument
01 LDI n   02 ADD n   03 SUB n   04 LDA a
05 STA a   06 JMP i   07 JZ i   08 JNZ i
09 OUT     0A HLT     0B IN     00 NOP
(jump targets count instructions, not bytes)

Program library: every ROM streams its bytes
into its download link once at startup.
Download a .bin, then upload it via the file
input on the front panel to run it.

hello_world: prints text + a counted loop
count: prints 0..9
cowsay: type a name first, then RUN
calc: type e.g. 3+4 or 8-5 first, then RUN
(single digits; minus expects first >= second)

Text input: the IN instruction (0B) flushes one
typed character, the latch holds it for the CPU.
A flush on an empty buffer latches 0 —
programs detect the end of input via JZ.
Type the text before flipping RUN.
